athlete.name: James Bomba
athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with a knack for acrobatic catches, this tight end blends agility and strength, embodying a team-first mentality. Off the field, his infectious energy inspires teammates and fans alike.

caption:
Indiana football has been part of my life for as long as I can remember. My dad and both my grandpas played here. My dad coached here. After five years, I can now say I lived out the dream they inspired me to achieve. Putting that jersey on every week meant more than just football. It was about honoring those who came before me. That responsibility shaped me, challenged me, and made every moment in that uniform unforgettable.

To finish my career as an Undefeated National Champion is something I never dreamed of. To my teammates from this year, you guys made this journey even more special.

This chapter of my life is finished, but my love for this place will never change. I’m thankful for every teammate, every coach, and every memory along the way. I will always bleed Cream and Crimson. Never Daunted. Go Hoosiers.

caption:
Holiday Season is always a time reflection:

Headed into the new year I just wanted to acknowledge the fact that you could never forget where you came from and the people along the way that sparked the dream that you get to chase. It’s a blessing to be able to use my talents to be in positions where I can give back to the people who are in the same shoes I walked in and honestly just show them that is possible. I wasn’t a heavily recruited Player in high school and to be honest when I first got there I really wasn’t that good but with time and effort and obsession you can honestly achieve anything you set your mind to. This is just a reminder of that for me. Keep Chasing kid. You never know what could happen.

Where do you go from there:

When you see potential it’s your job to nurture it. That means being patient with the process. Taking things slow and working consistently on the right things.

As a player it’s your job to take information and apply it. If you only work on your game when you are at the gym it’s not enough. The real growth happens at home. In the store. At the park.

Wherever you can rehearse the things you have been learning and you will see them come to fruition in real life.

athlete.name: Ava Vickers
athlete.bio: A tenacious playmaker with a fierce competitive spirit, this Indiana standout excels at orchestrating offense and dominating the paint. Off the court, her infectious enthusiasm unites teammates and fans alike.

caption:
Pain, Patience & Perseverance: Episode 1 releasing this Sunday on my YouTube Channel🤍 
 I truly believe the challenges life throws at you are just an opportunity for you to become stronger. Going through injury this past year forced me to sit with a kind of stillness I wasn’t used to — physically, mentally, and emotionally. I had to watch from the sidelines, support from the bench, and learn to show up for my team in ways that didn’t involve scoring points. But with going through all of this I was growing. 
I was learning what it means to be a leader off the court. I was learning how to stay present. I was learning that perseverance doesn’t always look like grinding in the gym, sometimes it looks like rest, reflection, and showing up anyway.
This chapter taught me lessons I didn’t know I needed. And now I’m excited to share that story. 
Pain, Patience & Perseverance: Episode 1 drops this Sunday on my YouTube channel!

caption:
Happy September 1st Eve !!!

To all the juniors out there anxiously awaiting tomorrow, I just want to take a moment to remind you of something really important: whether your phone rings the second it turns midnight, or if it doesn’t ring at all, you are still a successful athlete and worthy of your sport.

September 1 can feel like a huge day, and for some it will be. But your worth as an athlete isn’t determined by whether you get a call on that exact day. Some athletes get their first call the moment the clock strikes midnight, others much later — sometimes not until senior year, maybe even in the middle of spring break. And you know what? Both paths are equally valid and both lead to success.

So if you don’t hear from a coach tomorrow, please don’t let it steal your joy or make you doubt your journey. What truly matters is the work you put in, the heart you bring to the game, and your willingness to keep pushing forward. The right coaches will recognize your talent and your drive — sometimes it just takes a little longer for them to find you.

Hold your head high, be proud of how far you’ve come, and remember: no matter what happens on September 1, you belong, and your story is still being written.

Keep working, keep believing, and let tomorrow be one step in your journey — not the definition of it. Write your own story, don’t try to live others. 

#explore #softball #fastpitch #softballlife #reels #indiana #d1 #dr3fastpitch #d1softball #september1

caption:
When you need more, you learn more. And when you keep learning, you keep growing. 

This week in July was a full-circle moment. Let me explain… I brought  one of my Power 4 pitchers, Meg, to work with one of my mentors who has shaped me as a coach.

For years, I’ve been learning from Esia—studying movement, observing, and growing not only in my coaching but also as a person. To sit in, learn in-person, and bring Meg alongside me was powerful.

Here’s the truth: every coach has strengths, but also limits. The best coaches admit it, collaborate, and seek out people who can help their athletes grow beyond what we can give. That’s why I send my pitchers to him when I know it’s time for that next layer. And when my pitchers take advantage of working with him? The growth is undeniable.

Thank you, Esia, for being a wonderful role model and challenger—not just for me, but for the athletes who get the chance to work with you.

This is what it’s all about—never arriving, always evolving. 

#fastpitch #softball #pitching #texas

athlete.name: Megan Gregory
athlete.bio: A fierce competitor with a keen strategic mind, this pitcher wields an arsenal of pitches that confound hitters. Off the field, her infectious energy and humor unite teammates, fostering camaraderie.

caption:
From Day One to D1.
Megan Gregory walked into her first lesson with only six months of pitching experience—and a fire in her eyes. She was 14 years old, brand new to the circle, and ready to put in the work. That was back in 2020, just after I moved to Canton, GA and started building DR3 Fastpitch.

Since then, we’ve been side-by-side through every season—through the ups, the setbacks, the grind, the breakthroughs. From high school bullpens to college breaks… now she’s a junior pitcher at a Power Four program: Indiana University.

Watching Megan grow mentally, physically, emotionally—it’s been nothing short of incredible. Every “no” that came her way? She turned it into fuel. Every door that closed? She built her own. Discipline. Grit. Focus. Determination. She’s a role model for pitchers everywhere—and a prime example of what happens when you don’t just dream big… you work big.

Now, she travels with me, pours into other young athletes, and continues to LEVEL UP. I’m beyond proud and beyond grateful to have her in my corner.

This is what it looks like to own your journey.

caption:
Stop thinking about the last pitch & assuming the worst for the next pitch 😤 
.
Stay present; easier said than done, I know. It takes practice like anything else. 
.
Give yourself a few, like 3, seconds to process the pitch you just threw. It shouldn’t take long —> move on. Now we’re being present. We’re going to use our visualization skills and positive self talk for this current pitch. We’re going to give it 100% of our effort and attention. Now we’re going to rinse & repeat.
.
There’s typically over 100 pitches you’re going throw in a game and that’s why this is a skill that needs to be practiced; it’s exhausting at first! Like anything though, with time and effort, you can master and condition this 🙌 
.
You owe it to yourself 😘 start now! #paisleyspitching #pitchers #pitchinglessons #pitchingcoach #pitch #pitcher

caption:
Watch me as I do all 4 services at Restore for my optimal recovery routine!

First up is cryotherapy for 3 minutes at -202F degrees. This therapy helps reduce the swelling & inflammation in my body especially after those long training days! 

Right after cryo, I jump into red light therapy which has the same healing properties as cryo, but the red light is helping improve circulation and expanding my blood vessels so you can instantly feel the recovery happening as you’re standing in between the red light panels.

Next up, I have 1 hr long with compression leg sleeves. These are amazing for your limbs to encourage blood flow and circulation, and breaking up that lactic acid.  It’s the perfect way to get rid of my aches & pain.

Lastly, I sweated and detoxed in their infrared sauna for 1 hr. It’s a great service for my skin, muscles, and heart. Plus, I sleep like a baby after sweating out all those heavy metals!

Combining these services is truly the way to reduce those recovery days in between heavy weight lifting and conditioning non stop. Restore also offers other special services to help make you feel rejuvenated & restored. Don’t forget about their student discount, all of these services only for $21!
